research.validation: Existing X-11 reproductions compare the local booster against source home_wp as a diagnostic and record feature/training protocol hashes.

Compute diagnostic play-state win probability
Orient the output to the X-13 focal team
independently_reproduced: REPRO-X11-NFL-FASTRMODELS-V1 and V2 are registered locally with frozen protocols.

source.provenance_notes: The author submission is titled 'Swiper, No Swiping: Measuring High Quality Interception Opportunity Creation' and states that it measures defender-created interception opportunity at ball arrival rather than only recorded turnovers.

research.research_question: How often does a defender create a high-quality interception opportunity even when no interception is recorded?
inputs: Player and ball tracking at ball arrival
research.target: Interception-opportunity quality rather than the observed interception label alone.
research.validation: Not independently verified from an executable source; any SAF adaptation would require a new registered target and game-grouped validation.

reusable_portion: Do not collapse opportunity quality into realized turnover outcome
Use expected-versus-observed decomposition for rare events
independently_reproduced: No HQIO result or model reproduced.
prohibited_uses: Do not download or copy the writeup code or tracking data until licenses are verified.
Do not create turnover-over-expected from X-13 observed turnover taxonomy.

No PIT interception-opportunity probability exists in the frozen feature view.
Exact implementation and validation details were not independently verified.
evidence_boundary.claim_boundary: Conceptual warning against outcome-only turnover factors; no HQIO metric enters the current factor universe.

research.target: Five-class punt outcome and expected field position, with expected-versus-observed field position or EPA.

Model expected post-punt field position before comparing realized outcome
Use a chronological held-out season

research.research_question: On fourth down, how does the chosen go, field-goal, or punt action compare with the action having the highest modeled win probability?
research.target: go_wp, fg_wp, punt_wp, best action, go_boost, and chosen-minus-best decision regret.
research.validation: Run once in a pinned R environment, preserve input and package hashes, convert output to hashed Parquet, and compare fixed fourth-down fixtures before joining markets.

reusable_portion: Offline action-conditional win probabilities
Chosen action versus best action comparison
Documented edge-case limitations
independently_reproduced: Not yet reproduced in this worktree because the isolated R build step is not installed; the method and version are frozen for that build.
prohibited_uses: Do not call regret a coaching error without checking documented edge cases.
Do not compute with post-play state or market reaction.

data_gaps: Pinned R runtime and hashed nfl4th output Parquet are not yet present.
Model limitations include player, penalty, weather, return, and blocked-kick cases.
evidence_boundary.claim_boundary: Registered diagnostic decision factor pending the isolated build; no fourth-down result exists until hashed output passes fixtures.

research.validation: Use only frozen columns, verify field orientation and pre/post semantics with fixtures, and keep source-computed outputs separate from independently fitted SAF models.

prohibited_uses: Do not treat source-computed WP as prediction-market fair value.
Do not use final revised outcome fields as pre-event features.

cards.title: nflfastR expected pass and pass over expected

source.provenance_notes: Official add_xpass documentation defines xpass as dropback probability in [0,1] and pass_oe as dropback percent over expected scaled to 100; frozen DS-NFLVERSE already contains both.

code.notes: The containing nflfastR v5.2.0 source is MIT.

data.notes: The local xpass and pass_oe fields are read from frozen DS-NFLVERSE.

research.research_question: Was a dropback surprising given the pre-play game state, distinct from whether the realized pass succeeded?
research.validation: Verify xpass range, pass_oe scaling, missingness before 2006, and focal-team orientation; never validate it against realized yards.

reusable_portion: Use xpass as expected play-call probability
Use pass_oe as play-choice surprise
Keep choice surprise separate from realized EPA, yards, and turnover
independently_reproduced: Frozen 2025 DS-NFLVERSE contains xpass and pass_oe; the factor pipeline validates their range and uses source values without refitting.
prohibited_uses: Do not call pass_oe pass quality, yards surprise, or turnover surprise.
Do not use post-play outcome when forming the pre-play choice feature.

data_gaps: The expected-pass model is not independently retrained in SAF.
Source training coverage and exact event-time model availability are not re-proven.
evidence_boundary.claim_boundary: Diagnostic play-choice surprise only; market residual and alpha claims require separate registered tests.
